complexity.notes: Counting is non-idiomatic (`num in num_counts` then a second lookup; `dict.get(num, 0) + 1` or `collections.Counter` is cleaner), and the O(k*m) reverse lookup plus list(set(...)) dedup is convoluted — sorting items by count or using a heap would be simpler and faster. Correctness hinges on the statement's unique-answer precondition: if a frequency tie straddled the k-th boundary, the value-based reverse lookup would emit more than k keys.
complexity.summary: Builds a frequency dict, sorts the frequency values and keeps the top k, then reverse-looks-up every key whose count matches one of those frequencies and dedups via set().
